sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Borealis's Mist** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 158% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 474% of Incantation Scaling and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most expensive one, but it effectively combines the high Frostbite build-up of Dragonice with the higher Magic damage of Ghostflame Breath.
 - Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP.
 - Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 6% less damage and consumes 17% more FP but causes 100% more Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 168 FP: 2*48 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 91 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the second weakest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 16% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and 7% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 2% more damage than Ekzykes's Decay.
 - However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
 - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- Agheel's Flame, a stronger Fire damage version of this spell
- Dragonice, a weaker but cheaper version of this spell
- Ekzykes's Decay, a weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot
- Ghostflame Breath, a slightly stronger Magic damage version of this spell that inflicts less Frostbite
- Smarag's Glintstone Breath, a stronger Magic damage version of this spell that doesn't inflict Frostbite

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Briars of Punishment** is a sorcery spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the thorn sorceries.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Mountaintops of the Giants
- Located by a dead tree on the western cliffs of the southern end of the giant stone bridge surrounded by Guilty enemies.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: The caster sacrifices their own blood to summon crawling vines of bloodthorn that pursue a single target. This spell deals Magic damage with an Attack Power equal to 212% of Sorcery Scaling, inflicting 72 Blood Loss and 7 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 50 HP and applies 25 Blood Loss per cast or recast.
- Costs 9 FP per cast or recast.
- Costs 22 Stamina per cast or recast.
- This spell has a long range and can scale walls and other obstacles.
- This spell will track and home in on its target.
- This spell utilizes the Briars of Sin.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown:
- Alberich's Bracers, Alberich's Robe, Alberich's Pointed Hat, and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) each boost the effectiveness by 6%, up to a maximum of 18%.
- Staff of the Guilty boosts the Attack Power by 20%.
- Magic Scorpion Charm increases Magic Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Magic Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes.
- Albinauric Staff and Maternal Staff provide a scaling bonus to Blood Loss buildup based on the caster's Arcane attribute.
- Azur's Glintstone Staff reduces the casting time of spells.
- Lord of Blood's Exultation boosts attack power by 20% (12% in PvP) for 20 seconds when Blood Loss occurs nearby.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown: - Briars of Punishment fires fewer projectiles than Impenetrable Thorns but is more reliable at long range against single targets.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Requires Faith rather than Intelligence.
- Patch 1.07 reduced the FP cost from 13 to 9, increased the on-hit Blood Loss from 60 to 72, and reduced the casting time.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Crouch down to raise a series of pillars of flame around the caster, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 288% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.markdown:

- Charging the spell only slightly increases the casting time.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- This spell is quite devastating against large targets who may be struck by multiple pillars.
- Since the caster kneels down when casting they are harder to hit for some chest- or head-height attacks.
- Smaller, humanoid enemies (Melenia, Any Footsoldier, etc...) will be thrown into the air after being hit by a pillar.

- This spell draws upon the same power as other Giants' Flame Incantations.
- Patch 1.07: Reduced FP consumption. Shortened the time it takes for a flame pillar to be generated.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: The caster channels for 3 seconds before releasing a torrent of energy that deals Magic damage, with an Attack Power equal to ???% of Sorcery Scaling per second. The beam continues as long as the casting button is held, consuming additional FP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 46 FP per cast and drains 10 FP per sustained increment.
- Costs 34 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 3 Memory Slots to equip.
- Can be channeled until FP is depleted.
- Deals low Stance damage, but the beam's end deals more.

sections.heading: Boosting

- Azur's Glintstone Crown boosts attack power and FP cost by 15%.
- Azur's Glintstone Staff reduces casting time and increases FP costs by 20%.
- Cerulean Hidden Tear removes FP costs for 15 seconds.
- Glintstone Scarab reduces FP cost by 15%.
- The Graven-School Talisman and Graven-Mass Talisman boost attack power by 4% and 8% respectively, stacking for a total of 12%.
- Magic Scorpion Charm boosts attack power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear boosts attack power by 20% (15% in PvP).
- Primal Glintstone Blade reduces FP cost by 25%.
- Radagon Icon reduces casting time by ??%.
- Terra Magica boosts attack power by 35%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The beam has long range and can pass through enemies.
- The beam’s direction cannot be adjusted once cast.
- Casting time is reduced by Dexterity, up to a maximum of 70 Dexterity.
- If cast immediately after applying the Cerulean Hidden Tear, it can be channeled without FP drain for up to 12 seconds.
- This spell is easily interrupted due to its long casting time.
- Most bosses and enemies will dodge when the spell is initially cast, not when the beam is released.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Castle Morne** is a location in Elden Ring. Found at the southernmost point in the Lands Between, it overlooks the southeastern shore of the Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Castle Morne once belonged to the Stormveil faction that later fell to the Erdtree long ago. A clan of warriors rose against Queen Marika, only to be vanquished. The lone survivor, burdened by anger and regret, collected their swords and reforged them into a single Grafted Blade Greatsword. Morne was the site of their legendary showdown with Godfrey, First Elden Lord, commemorated by a nearby Sword Monument. Although the hero swore an Oath of Vengeance, they were ultimately defeated by the Elden Lord, and their sword became a treasure of the keep.

After the Shattering, this fortress fell under the control of Godrick the Grafted, a distant scion of the Golden Lineage, who ruled Limgrave from Stormveil Castle. He appointed Castellan Edgar to oversee the castle and its Godrick Soldier garrison; however, by the time the player arrives, it has fallen to an uprising by its maltreated Misbegotten servants. Edgar's blind daughter, Irina of Morne, fled the castle, but her Great Coffin escort was overtaken by Misbegotten on the road near the Bridge of Sacrifice. Edgar is bound by duty to maintain his post until the sword of Morne is reclaimed from the Leonine Misbegotten.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- In heraldry, *morné* (or *morne*) describes a beast, typically a lion, depicted standing fiercely on one hind leg with its forepaws elevated, without teeth, claws, or a tongue. The term derives from the Old French *morner* ("to blunt"), representing a defanged, defeated, or stripped-down state. The name "Castle Morne" likely describes the castle's recurring themes of loss and diminished power, including the golden lion emblazoned on the vanquished revenger's Grafted Blade Greatsword, the rebellion of the oppressed Leonine Misbegotten who seized that weapon, the prior conquest of the castle by Godfrey, and the suppression of Godfrey's true ferocity by Serosh, Lord of Beasts. It may also allude to Stormveil stormhawks or Elder Lions, whose respective talons and horns were amputated by Godfrey's Golden Lineage. Although stormhawks are absent from the castle, their likeness appears on palisades throughout its grounds.
- Mentioned in *Dark Souls III*, Morne was a knight who served the goddess of tears.

sections.markdown: Castellan Edgar**, later known as **Edgar the Revenger**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Edgar was one of the Banished Knights, members of a defeated army who were driven from their home and sent to the fringes of the Lands Between. During or after the Shattering, he was appointed commander of Castle Morne by Godrick the Grafted, the Lord of Limgrave, who entrusted him with safeguarding its storied sword. Edgar lived there with his daughter, Irina, until the Misbegotten servants rebelled and overran the castle. Irina and a number of other inhabitants fled the keep, but Edgar and a retinue of Godrick Soldiers stubbornly stayed behind to prevent the Grafted Blade Greatsword from falling into the wrong hands.

The Tarnished may arrive at Castle Morne at the behest of Irina. Once the Misbegotten rebels are vanquished and the treasured weapon is reclaimed, Edgar is no longer bound to the castle. He soon departs, promising to spend the rest of his days with Irina, only to find that the Misbegotten have murdered her before he arrives. A grief-stricken Edgar vows to punish those responsible for his daughter's killing.

Edgar hunts the Misbegotten across the continent on his quest for vengeance, and eventually succumbs to madness. He later invades the Tarnished at the Revenger's Shack in Liurnia of the Lakes as an invader. Upon his death, Edgar bequeaths his Shabriri Grape, the eyeball of one consumed by frenzy.

sections.markdown: Castellan Jerren**, also known as **Witch-Hunter Jerren**, is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Jerren is the elderly castellan of Redmane Castle. In the past, Jerren was a nomadic warrior who became a guest of the Carian Royal Family. There, he became acquainted with General Radahn, the son of Radagon and Rennala, the Carian queen, who would later challenge the stars and arrest their movements, halting fate. He was considered an eccentric by Smithing Master Iji, the troll war counselor of the Carians. During this time, Jerren made a promise to kill Sellen, the Graven Witch, a sorceress who had long been a hindrance to the Carians.

After spending time as a guest of the Carians, Jerren served as a guest commander under General Radahn, and the two swore an oath of honourable death to one another. During the Shattering, Radahn fought Malenia, Blade of Miquella in the Battle of Aeonia, and in the aftermath was driven mad by Malenia's rot, cursed to wander the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike. Jerren convened the Radahn Festival to give Radahn a warrior's death.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
He attracted champions from across the Lands Between to participate in a battle against the Red Lion General and a chance to claim his Great Rune. Among the champions who converge upon Redmane Castle to participate in the festival is the Tarnished who succeeds in defeating Radahn, giving him an honourable death.

With Radahn dead, the stars are once again set into motion, and Sellen is dispossessed of her immortality. Finally able to uphold his old promise, Jerren travels to Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, where Sellen is bound by the Academy's shackles. When he arrives, he finds her as a husk, her soul having seemingly already fled. Suspecting Sellen to still be alive somewhere, Jerren continues his hunt, eventually tracking her down to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He vows to kill her and crush her Primal Glintstone, which facilitated her survival. Should the Tarnished aid him in defeating Sellen, he will thank them before departing, promising to meet them again at the next tournament.

 - Jerren can be encountered in Redmane Castle before initiating the Radahn Festival, sitting on a chair inside the church just beyond the Redmane Castle Plaza. Speaking to him here will unlock some additional dialogue with War Counselor Iji.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Brother Corhyn** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring. He can be given prayerbooks to access an array of Incantations.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order. At some point, Corhyn made his way to Roundtable Hold, where he teaches the incantations of the Two Fingers to Tarnished of the Roundtable, hoping that one of them might one day claim the title of Elden Lord, so that Corhyn might council them. When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable, Corhyn introduces himself to them, and offers his tutelage. Corhyn will even teach the champion heretical incantations, from outside the line of the Erdtree, though he does so reluctantly.

After the Tarnished champion opens the way to the Altus Plateau, Corhyn announces that he is departing the Roundtable to search for the legendary Goldmask, an eminent scholar of the Golden Order. While searching for Goldmask, Corhyn continues his own investigations into the nature of the Golden Order, and while he makes some advancements, he also becomes aware of how little he truly knows. With guidance from the Tarnished champion, Corhyn is united with Goldmask.

Corhyn takes it upon himself to become Goldmask's disciple and to chronicle his wisdom, deciphering the meaning behind every minute movement made by the mute Goldmask. The process goes well, until Goldmask's movements suddenly cease, as he is confounded by the nature of Radagon. The Tarnished champion may solve the riddle, revealing to Goldmask that Radagon and Queen Marika the Eternal are in fact one and the same, allowing Corhyn to continue his work.

Goldmask leads his disciple to the Forbidden Lands and the Mountaintops of the Giants, where none may tread. Corhyn continues his duty, but begins to doubt his master. He detects in his movements that Goldmask has begun to suspect the holism of the Golden Order, an unacceptable heresy in Corhyn's mind. Corhyn continues to serve his master, but is tormented by doubt.

After the Tarnished champion unleashes the flame of the giants to burn the Erdtree, Corhyn is found in the ashen ruins of Leyndell, Royal Capital. Corhyn denounces his master as nothing more than a madman, who rejected the perfection of the Golden Order and sought to replace it with his own "perfected" order. As the Erdtree burns above him, Corhyn loses his mind. Alternatively, Corhyn may be offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, causing him to remain in the Mountaintops, seemingly unaware that Goldmask has returned to Leyndell.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Castle Sol was an old fortress built on the northernmost tip of the Lands Between, belonging to those who later became Banished Knights. These drake hunters would gift an Icerind Hatchet, made from a scale of Borealis the Freezing Fog, to Liurnia of the Lakes as part of their diplomatic relationships.

In the distant past, a frigid, awe-inspiring eclipse mesmerized the knights of Castle Sol. Drained of its color, the lusterless sun repelled Destined Death and granted life to the soulless. The castle's inhabitants gathered at its Church of the Eclipse, where they used the storied Eclipse Shotel in worship of the dreadful celestial event.

In a later age, when veteran Commander Niall and his men were garrisoned at Sol, another force defeated them in battle even though they wielded storm and lightning-clad weapons. In exchange for the captured lives of his fallen men, Niall offered his right leg. Unable to die, and with nowhere to fade to, Niall eternally led the summoned spirits of his army of no nation.

Following the Night of Black Knives, Sol's inhabitants fervently prayed for another eclipse, hoping to call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. The Mausoleum Knights, who beheaded themselves to protect their masters as spirits, displayed the Eclipse to ward off the Destined Death of Godwyn the Golden.

Later, Miquella the Kind visited to castle and petitioned the master to return the life of his comrade. He bestowed half of a secret medallion to the master that would allow him to access the then-upcoming Haligtree if he had succeeded in his task. However, the awaited eclipse never came to pass, making the master of the castle unable to visit the Haligtree as he wasn't able to fulfill his duty, thus he lost hope and perished. Niall, the commander of Castle Sol, left alone in the castle to protect his long-passed master, continue commanding the nationless spirits of his Banished Knight army.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Cleanrot Knights were fierce warriors who remained devoted to Malenia, Blade of Miquella, even as her scarlet rot consumed their bodies. Their winged helms and sword insignias embodied the unyielding resolve of their Empyrean master. They stood in arms with Miquella's followers within Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

They fought under Malenia's command throughout her undefeated campaign in the Shattering, which culminated in the fateful clash against General Radahn's Redmane army in Caelid. A majority of the knights fell at the Battle of Aeonia, their spirits locked in eternal combat in the War-Dead Catacombs. The few survivors wandered the resulting Swamp of Aeonia, while others traced the footsteps of Cleanrot Knight Finlay, who bore the sleeping Malenia all the way back to the Haligtree, passing through the Shaded Castle along the way.

sections.heading: Chacteristics
sections.markdown: All Cleanrot Knights wear golden armor and wield a Cleanrot Knight's Sword as a secondary weapon to complement their polearms. This allows them to land multiple attacks in quick succession, triggering the Talisman's blessing to strengthen them even further. Most Cleanrot Knights wield a Cleanrot Spear, which bears a small shield on its shaft. They will imbue their spear with gold before performing their more deadly attacks, such as grabbing their enemy with the spear tip and infecting them with Scarlet Rot, and summoning forth a golden palisade from the ground. They can also brace their spear with their sword to absorb an incoming blow and quickly retaliate with their own. Cleanrot knight commanders wield the Halo Scythe. They prefer ranged combat, repeatedly firing rings of Miquella's light from a distance. In close quarters, they may vomit Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.markdown: Cleanrot Knights are resistant to Slash and Holy damage, taking 35% and 40% less damage from these types. They receive flat damage from Pierce and Lightning damage, but take 20% extra damage from Fire attacks; however, the scythe-wielding variant can nullify this vulnerability by casting an incantation.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
An old, crumbling church on the eastern side of Liurnia of the Lakes. The Church of Vows was the site of the marriage between Rennala, Queen of Caria, and Radagon, the red-haired champion of the Golden Order, uniting the houses of the Erdtree and the Moon following their conflict during the Second Liurnian War. Several of Radagon's personal effects are found at this location, seemingly abandoned as part of his vow.

The aged tortoise pastor, Miriel, oversees the church despite its dilapidated state. He has in-depth knowledge of the history of Liurnia and the Carian Royal Family, which he is happy to divulge if spoken to.

sections.heading: Basin of Atonement
sections.markdown:
At the back of the church stands a Nox Swordstress statue and an ornate Basin of Atonement. It is said that Radagon repented his territorial aggression by cleansing himself with dew in this pool. The player may replicate this act here by offering up Celestial Dew, performing an Absolution.

Absolution simply reverts any NPCs that have been attacked and made hostile back to their original, non-hostile state. It will not render passive any characters that are hostile by default, nor will it revive those who have died. It will not restore Melina as a traveling companion, even if the Frenzied Flame has been suppressed with Miquella's Needle.

sections.markdown: The **Chapel of Anticipation** is a legacy dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Chapel of Anticipation is the first location the player explores when they begin the game. It consists of a small chapel connected by rope bridge to a wide-open courtyard featuring a large statue of Queen Marika. The path to Stormveil Castle and the rest of Limgrave has crumbled away, and a Grafted Scion is prepared to ambush any Tarnished who enter the courtyard.

After crossing the Sea of Fog, the Tarnished awakens beneath a maiden statue in the chapel. Their ill-starred Finger Maiden is slumped against the south wall, lying in a pool of her blood. Her body holds the Tarnished's Wizened Finger. An encouraging Message on the floor reads *"Though the path be broken and uncertain, claim your place as Elden Lord."* The room is exited through an operable door nearby.

sections.heading: Leaving
sections.markdown:
There are three ways to leave the Chapel of Anticipation:
1. Defeat the Grafted Scion
1. Be killed by the Grafted Scion
1. Fall from the cliff by walking near the Nascent Butterflies

Upon doing so, the player is transported to the Stranded Graveyard, where they are by rescued by Melina and Torrent.

sections.heading: Second visit
sections.markdown:
The player may revisit the area later via the *"Precipice of Anticipation"* Sending Gate at The Four Belfries in Liurnia of the Lakes. However, the teleporter must first be activated with an Imbued Sword Key. The destination point is on the side opposite the initial spawn point.

If the Grafted Scion was not defeated previously, it can be challenged once more. Additionally, the door at the side of the chapel will now be unlocked, allowing the player to collect Stormhawk Deenh and The Stormhawk King.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This weapon is wielded by the young maidens who play a central role in the festival.
- Grants 10 Runes every time an enemy is hit.
- The strongest dagger for the Keen affinity, with its A being just on the verge of an S-scaling. Otherwise somewhat subpar or average when it comes to damage, including the otherwise Dexterity-scaling Lightning and Cold affinities.
 - Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
 - Pairs well with non-physical affinities such as Magic since those are usually already only partially negated by guarding and the ignored guarding damage negation applies to all forms of damage, not just Physical.
 - As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information

- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
- Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
 - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Carian Study Hall** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Carian Study Hall is a building on the eastern coast of Liurnia, to the north of Jarburg. It is connected to the Divine Tower of Liurnia by a great bridge, though it is not accessible initially.

The Study Hall consists of a vast library spanning multiple storeys, accessed by an elevator from a chapel-like entrance hall. The study hall is patrolled by Preceptor Miriam, a sorceress who calls upon blue, spectral nobles and prefers to fight from a distance using magical projectiles.

The hall hides a secret, which is revealed when a Carian Inverted Statue is placed onto a pedestal of a celestial globe in the entrance hall. Doing so flips the entire building upside-down, leading to another encounter with Miriam and revealing the entrance to the Divine Tower of Liurnia.

The player receives the Carian Inverted Statue from Ranni the Witch after bringing her the Fingerslayer Blade. The Divine Tower beyond the study hall hides Ranni's true body, which bears the Cursemark of Death.

sections.heading: Study Hall Entrance
sections.markdown: Found in the entrance chamber at the start of the dungeon.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
For both versions of the area, the greatest danger will be dangerous ranged Magic attacks, so bringing some way to counteract that (such as Spellproof Dried Liver, Magic Fortification, or Spelldrake Talisman) is useful.

Normally only the Standard version is accessible but both versions can be freely switched between after acquiring the Carian Inverted Statue.

sections.heading: Standard version
sections.markdown:
From the only Grace, ignore the altar and walk around it. Take the elevator up to a split with stairs to a bridge on the left and a sidepath on the right. At the end of the sidepath is a Golden Rune [3] and picking up spawns two puppet Estoc variant Wandering Nobles.

Walking up the stairs spawns two more puppet Nobles and Preceptor Miriam. Hitting Miriam once or twice causes her to teleport further away, a behavior that will continue for the rest of the area until she is killed (though do note that she can skip over spots if enough damage is inflicted in one go). On the bridge itself 5 more Nobles will spawn as you approach Miriam on the other side, while she will snipe at you with Loretta's Greatbow.

The stairs at the other side of the bridge has Miriam and another puppet Noble and 2 more Nobles will spawn upon approaching a small raised stone section with the Carian Glintstone Staff. Further along and to the right is an elevator to the second floor.

The first level of the second floor is essentially a circular balcony where you play a game of ring-around-the-rosie with Preceptor Miriam and occasionally spawning puppet Nobles, now also with the sorcerer variant. Miriam will alternate between either using Loretta's Greatbow or Magic Downpour while teleporting clockwise around the area if you approach closely while she isn't charging a spell, so try to either attack her as the spell is being charged up or use a ranged weapon like a Bow. Since the puppets don't respawn until resting at a grace one may want to focus their first lap in killing them. Killing her gives the Magic Downpour sorcery and a Golden Rune [4] can be found on the ring.

To the left of the elevator used to come up and two lengths of the railing along is a ladder to the lower rafters. There is no item on the lower level but there are to Giant Rats, one straight ahead and one far to the right. Additionally there is another ladder up to the upper rafters, with 3 more Giant Rats and also the Cerulean Seed Talisman.

sections.heading: Inverted version
sections.markdown:
Using the Carian Inverted Statue on the altar instead changes the path behind it. The elevator well is now fall onto a ledge around a hole in the floor, and beyond it is a thin hole with 1 small Fingercreepers with another 2 flanking it on the walls.

Entering into the bridge room, which is now a set of walkways with a platform in the middle. Take a left to drop down to a nook with the Mask of Confidence while dropping down on the right takes you to 2 small Fingercreepers. Since Preceptor Miriam will be standing on the central platform and bombard you with Loretta's Greatbow and Magic Downpour, stick close to the wall when approaching. Two more small Fingercreepers are on the same platform and a spear-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldier puppet hides around a corner to support her. Reducing Miriam to half health causes her to teleport further away.

The Preceptor will stand across the gap, now unrestricted by cover, so keep an eye on her while dealing with the new enemies. Moving forward and to the right is a bridge with 2 Fingercreepers on it and a nook with a Fingercreeper to the right. Guarding Miriam final location will be 2 sword-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldiers that may have to be dealt with first. Defeat her to get Lucidity.

Since there are no more doors forward you instead have to either drop down to either the middle chandelier below you and then one below that or fall of the right side to the wooden walkway around the area. Either way lets you drop down to the rafters and some Giant Rats. The lower level of the rafters holds some Glintstone Fireflies on the central ring and a few Holyproof Dried Livers one the lower left offshoot beam (seen from Miriam's last spot).

Drop down into the elevator and use it to go down to access the door to Divine Tower of Liurnia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bosses** are powerful enemies that can be encountered in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Bosses can be found roaming the overworld or inside one of the many locations in the Lands Between. There are in total **238** bosses.

Several key indicators can identify a boss fight. Firstly, the music changes to a more intense or dramatic score. A health bar and the boss's name appear prominently at the bottom of the screen. Bosses yield a larger amount of Runes when defeated, and their items rewards are added directly to the inventory. Unlike common enemies, bosses are not revived when the player rests at a Site of Grace.

Some bosses appear out in the open world and will attack the player if they wander too close. These field bosses may be disengaged and fled from. The player can lead them a short distance away from their spawn points. Certain field bosses only appear at night: Deathbirds, Death Rite Birds, and Night's Cavalry.

If the player challenges the dungeon boss, they are trapped within the room by a fog wall until the boss is defeated. If the player is defeated, they may be required to pass through a fog gate to rechallenge the boss. Some difficult bosses may be encountered early on, which can drive player exploration.

sections.heading: Mandatory bosses
sections.markdown:
Over two hundred bosses are available to fight, but only a few must be beaten to finish the game. These bosses are encountered after acquiring two Great Runes and gaining access to Leyndell, Royal Capital.

1. Any two shardbearers: Godrick, Mohg, Rennala, Rykard, or Radahn
1. Draconic Tree Sentinel or Fia's Champions
1. Godfrey, First Elden Lord
1. Morgott, the Omen King

1. Godskin Duo

Two bosses must be defeated in order to access the *Shadow of the Erdtree*:

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Carian Royal Family** was a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Members of the Carian royal family were prolific Sorcerers and erstwhile heads of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, who were famous for developing their own glintstone sorceries. They originated from the mist-laden region in the west of the Lands Between, known as Liurnia of the Lakes.

The Carian royal family would reach its peak under Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. In her youth, she was a prominent champion who would go on to charm the academy with her lunar magic, becoming its master. She also led the Glintstone Knights and established the house of Caria as royalty.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Carian Royals have always been closely associated with the western coast of Liurnia, which is the location of their estate, the Caria Manor, as well as the Three Sisters immediately behind it. Another location of importance was the Carian Study Hall, a large library in eastern Liurnia that connects to the region's Divine Tower.

The Carian royals were served by magic preceptors notable for large hats with the movements of the stars drawn on the inside of the brim, as well as on their bright blue gowns. All glintstone sorcerers are the descendants of astrologers, a fact that the Carians remained aware of. The astrologers preceded the sorcerers and had established themselves in mountaintops that nearly touched the sky, and considered the Fire Giants their neighbors. They would read fate in the stars, but alas, the night sky no longer cradles fate.

However, the Carian royal family were mostly known for the famous enchanted knights that served them. These enchanted knights, anointed by the Lunar Queen, were heroes of the highest honors, and served as direct retainers to the kingdom's princesses. Their swords were embedded with blue glintstone, and could serve as catalysts, letting them wield sorcerous battle skills. Despite numbering fewer than twenty, this power made them a match for even the champions of gold in battle. They combined this art with their swordsmanship to maintain pressure upon their foes, striking in waves of steel and sorcery. The Carian knights never wavered, and even had sorceries that could alleviate the buildup of sleep or madness. There were also enchanted troll knights among their number, comrades of young Rennala, bound by oath. They were called into service when the Queen invoked an oath they swore. These trolls were treated as true knights of Caria, and would fight arm in arm with their human comrades.

The famous Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard to Carian royalty. Despite fighting mounted and using a war sickle, her favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow. She would leave her service in search of a haven for Albinaurics, but an apparition of her remains to defend Caria Manor to this day. Several Albinauric mages, such as Pidia, remained as servants to the Carian royal family, seemingly facing less persecution there then in other parts of the Lands Between.

The oldest sorcery devised by the Carians would conjure a Magic Glintblade, and it would serve as a prototype for more enhanced sword-phalanx sorceries wielded by royal enchanted knights. They also created sorceries that would conjure magic swords that could sweep, slice and pierce their enemies. Some sorceries were said to have been taught to them by the enigmatic Crystalians, to mark the swearing of an old concord.

Due to the influence of the Carians, the study of the primeval current was forbidden at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. However, the Lazuli Conspectus would eventually develop in the academy. The scholars of this conspectus sought to master Carian sorcery, and viewed the moon as equal to the stars. This would be seen as a heterodox pursuit, or even outright heresy, by their colleagues at the academy.

sections.heading: History
sections.markdown:
When Queen Marika the Eternal established her new Age of the Erdtree, she dispatched a champion known as Radagon to lead her armies against the lands of Liurnia. Not much was known about Radagon before he joined the ranks in the Liurnian Wars, but he was seen as a great champion with flowing red locks, and he would lead a great golden host to Liurnia, where he would meet Rennala in battle.

Radagon would fight two wars against Rennala and the Academy, both of which saw no clear victor. Instead, Radagon eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, swore his love to Rennala and became the husband of the Carian Queen.

He married her at the Church of Vows, and it would be this matrimonial union, and reconciliation between the houses of the Erdtree and the Full Moon that would eventually have grave consequences for the Carians, as it was during the age of the Erdtree that Carian astrology withered on the vine, as the fate once writ in the night skies had been fettered by the Golden Order.

Rennala would bequeath Radagon with a greatsword, to honor a long standing tradition in which a Moon Greatsword is bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse. Upon entering into marriage with Rennala and joining the Carian line, Radagon would order Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private. While husband to Rennala, he studied glintstone sorcery taught at the Academy. Together, Radagon and Rennala would go on to have three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.

After Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon left Rennala to become the second husband and King Consort of Queen Marika, and would receive the title of second Elden Lord. Queen Marika made Radagon's and Rennala's children her demigod stepchildren. When Radagon left, Rennala's heart left with him. Realizing their heartbroken queen was no champion at all, the Academy rebelled against the Carian royal family and Rennala would find herself under the assault of her own students, who would eventually lock her away in the grand library.

Liurnia decended in civil war, with the Carians and their retainers on one side, and the Academy and its Knights of the Cuckoo on the other. The soldiers of Raya Lucaria were known as the Cuckoos, as their symbol was a peering cuckoo bird, the bird's shrewd gaze an expression of their refusal to be mere servants of the academy. They were given free rein by the scholars of the academy to wage war as they pleased, and they were infamous for their rapacious ways*.* The Knights of the Cuckoo would use "faux sorceries" and would be taught lesser spells by the academy as payment for their contract. Meanwhile, the Carian royal family had secretly been preparing against the disloyalty of the academy by devising sorceries that could dispel incoming spells and retaliate with glintblades. The moon and stars would go their separate ways.

The war would eventually lead to the Siege of Caria Manor. The Carians were taken off guard, but their strength had not yet fully waned, and they managed to repel the onslaught by conjuring a powerful enchanted snare that remains potent to this day.

sections.heading: Current Events
sections.markdown: As the Lands Between fell into disarray, the last Carian Princess, Ranni, made her way back to her family's ancestral home, where she would gather her allies and vassals in order to set her own plans into motion. Her vassals included her faithful shadow, the Half-Wolf Blaidd, her families old troll blacksmith Iji, who was now her war counsellor, as well as Seluvis, a preceptor in the sorcerous arts. She also won the loyalty of Glintstone Dragon Adula who swore a knightly oath to her and now guards the path to her tower. The Tarnished can join the group and eventually become her consort as she ushers in her Age of the Stars.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Claws** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Description
sections.markdown:
Claws are hand-held weapons consisting of one or more blades extending from the knuckles of the wielder. They are similar to Fists in terms of their attack patterns and range, though they scale primarily with Dexterity rather than Strength. Though they are shorter than most blades (ranging between that of Daggers and Straight Swords) and deal modest damage per hit, Claws excel at delivering rapid-fire, close-range slashing attacks that rend flesh easily. With the exception of the Venomous Fang, all Claws feature innate Bleed Damage.

Each Claw comes in a set of two, with the Tarnished wielding one on each hand when equipping a Claw "two-handed" without taking up both hand slots. When equipped one-handed, the Tarnished will hold one claw in one hand while the other is left tied to their belt.

sections.heading: Pros/Cons
sections.markdown:
- + Lightweight
- + Fast/high DPS
- + Can proc Blood Loss and other status effects quickly (if applied)
- + Paired Weapons - can be wielded in both hands with only one slot
- - Short Reach
- - Only four kinds available/cannot be farmed within the same playthrough (I.E. if a player wants to dual-wield two sets of the same type of Claws, they will have to wait until NG+ to acquire another)
- - Few Ashes of War available

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Colossal Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
They have excellent reach and area coverage, along with high damage against both health and poise, at the cost of their high weight and slow attack speed. Its one-handed moveset's slow speed is at risk of getting parried; however, most moves of its two-handed moveset are completely un-parriable.

Most Colossal Swords require a decent amount of investment into the Strength attribute in order to be wielded; however, it's possible to still wield a colossal sword with less strength than listed through two-handing, as two-handing increases the player's effective Strength by 50%.
